assessment.diversity_evidence: All stories share the central problem of a shivering animal stranded on a high ledge and end with it wrapped in a warm blanket. Most use the same bread-in-basket-and-rope rescue (for example, s000014 and s000041); only s000034, s000002, s000039, and s000035 use a ladder instead. Character and animal substitutions do not change the plot, and the ladder branch is a small causal variation. These sampled stories are highly similar, without establishing the diversity of the full generator.

assessment.diversity_evidence: The set centers on one garden problem: a broken tap, scarce water, and fallen shade. Most stories share the sunflower-first path, leaving a brown leaf and making a promise (s000002, s000023, s000058); a smaller branch waters tomatoes first, then uses the repaired tap for the sunflower (s000017, s000028). A few divide the water and shelter both plants under an umbrella (s000007, s000014). These are limited variations within a shared structure, and the prose is highly repetitive. This small sample does not establish the diversity of the entire generator.
